main_text.p: inita, armis in Saracenos & hostes Christiani nomĩs minus parārent. Quod nisi fecisset Palæologus, & promissum seruaret unionem, Carolo Siciliæ regi imperium Ioannis assignaret. Pollicebatur, & ex stella præsago ebat sibi longam vitam homo stolidus, & diu se victurum omnibus prædicabat: quippe cuius vita & mores omnibus patebant, adeoque erat inuerecundi & socordiæ ingenii. Sed ecce, dum hanc stultitiam coram suis iactaret, camera quaedam nova (aulam luxoriam Valerius vocat, stellatum preciosum thalamum) quam in palatio Viterbiensi ad delicias extruxerat, post quartum diem anno Domini 1277. subito corruit. Atque inter ligna & lapides soluti inuentus, septimo die post ruinam, & Pontifi-catus sui mense octauo, mi- serè interiit, in minori templo sepultus. Siceli prae-sagij uanitatem nunquam expertus: uacauit sedes per contentionem sex mensibus. Scripsit de problematibus quaedam, Aristotelem imitatus: Canones medicinæ, Thesaurum pauperum, & Epistolas.
main_text.head: 129 NICOLAVS tertius.
main_text.p: Nicolaus tertius, patria Romanus, de gente Ursina, Ioannes Caietanus, ante appellatus, protractus in sex menses electione, non sine magno puratorum patrum litibus, Papalem sedem occupabat.

page.notes: The first paragraph is a fragment that begins mid-sentence and carries cont="true". Several words at the line ends are cut by the scan and read with doubt, notably the word after "nomi" (the line break is in the scan), "Siceli" and "prae-sagij", and "occu" at the line end, which continues in the catchword "pabat,". The printed "Ioannis" and "Pollicebatur" were read from faint type. Margin fragments at the right edge (such as "Vr") are too faint to read and are not transcribed. The page number 322 and the running head were read clearly.
